text: Which platform was GSE309890 run on, and what organism is it?

## Abstract  
We queried the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) to identify the sequencing platform and study organism for the RNA-seq Series accession GSE309890. Using the automated `geo_series` tool, we retrieved the Series-level metadata without downloading bulky supplementary files. The record (UID = 200309890) reports a single platform (GPL24659) and lists “Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655” as the experimental organism. The Series comprises six RNA-seq samples. These results clarify the experimental context for downstream analyses or data reuse and demonstrate how a targeted programmatic query can rapidly surface essential metadata from GEO.

## I. Introduction  
Background.  Accurate knowledge of the experimental platform and organism is essential for interpreting transcriptomic datasets, ensuring correct choice of reference genomes, alignment parameters, and downstream analytical workflows.  
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap. The user needed confirmation of the sequencing platform and the organism used in GEO Series GSE309890, information not explicitly stated in the original question.  
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: Determine (i) the microarray/RNA-seq platform and (ii) the study organism for GEO Series GSE309890. We expected that GEO metadata would list both items explicitly.

## II. Materials and Methods  
Study Design. A single targeted metadata retrieval was sufficient; GEO’s E-utilities summary endpoint provides platform and organism fields for Series records.  
Materials.  
• GEO database (accessed via E-utilities API) – queried through the `geo_series` tool.  
Procedures.  
1. Tool call:  
   • `geo_series(accession="GSE309890", list_files=false)`  
   • Purpose: fetch Series-level metadata including `platform` and `taxon`.  
Statistical Analysis. No inferential statistics were required; values were taken verbatim from returned JSON fields.

## III. Results  
Data Presentation.  

Table 1. Key metadata for GEO Series GSE309890  
| Field | Value | Source field |  
|-------|-------|--------------|  
| Platform accession | GPL24659 | `platform` |  
| Organism (taxon) | Escherichia coli str. K-12 substr. MG1655 | `taxon` |  
| Experiment type | Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing | `experiment_type` |  
| Sample count | 6 | `sample_count` |  

Findings. GSE309890 was generated on platform GPL24659 and employed the bacterium Escherichia coli strain K-12 substrain MG1655 as the model organism.

## IV. Discussion  
Interpretation. The platform identifier (GPL24659) specifies the sequencing or library-preparation platform used, guiding researchers toward compatible analytical pipelines. The organism information confirms that the dataset pertains to a laboratory E. coli K-12 model, informing reference selection for alignment and downstream functional analyses.  
Context. These metadata align with the study’s focus on sertraline-induced antibiotic resistance in E. coli, as noted in the Series summary.  
Limitations. The GEO summary does not detail instrument model or library kit; such details may reside in the Platform (GPL24659) or Sample (GSM) records, or within supplementary files, which were not retrieved in this query.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. GSE309890 employs platform GPL24659 and investigates Escherichia coli K-12. Further work could extract the Platform record for protocol specifics and download the supplementary expression matrices to reproduce or extend the study’s analyses.

## References  
[1] GEO Series GSE309890 summary. https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE309890  
[2] NCBI E-utilities esummary call for UID 200309890. https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils/esummary.fcgi?db=gds&id=200309890&version=2.0  

## Acknowledgments  
We thank the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) for providing the GEO database and E-utilities web services.
